name: rand_read
purpose: Row-conflict lower bound: uniformly random addresses across the full mapped address space.
description: 8000 AR (read) transactions on one core, one AXI id (0), 64 bytes each, addresses drawn uniformly from [0, 2^31) and aligned down to a 64-byte boundary.

2^31 bytes is the full span reachable by this config's row/bankgroup/bank mapping (row bits [11:26], bankgroup [27:28], bank [29:30] -- 31 bits total, i.e. addr bits 0..30), so a uniform draw over that range spreads roughly evenly across all 16 banks (4 bankgroups x 4 banks) and, within a bank, essentially never repeats the same row twice in a row (1-in-65536 chance) -- almost every access should be a row conflict, and the very first access to each bank should be the only 'empty'.
numbers_in_prose: Numbers quoted in description/sanity_checks are from the run at authoring time and are NOT kept in sync with the model; they explain the reasoning, not the current values. golden.json holds the current numbers. The reasoning is what should be re-checked when a value moves -- if it no longer holds, that is a finding.

rng.draw: addr = (state >> 32) mod 2^31, then masked to a 64-byte boundary
rng.why_not_stdlib: std::rand and unseeded/version-dependent engines are not guaranteed to produce the same bit stream across platforms or standard-library versions; this LCG's three constants and 64-bit wraparound are the entire specification, so its output is reproducible anywhere that re-implements this file.

observed_metrics: see golden.json in this directory -- it is the authoritative snapshot, regenerated with --update-golden whenever model behavior deliberately changes. Numbers were duplicated here once and silently went stale the first time the timing model was fixed.
sanity_checks: row_empty_rate_pct (0.2%) is close to 16/8000 = 0.2% -- exactly matches 'one empty per bank on first touch', confirming addresses really do spread across all 16 banks as intended
page_hit_rate_pct == 0% is the expected worst case for i.i.d. uniform addressing -- OK

bankgroup_reuse_rate_pct (25.8%) is close to the 1-in-4 chance of two independent uniform draws landing in the same bankgroup, unlike seq_read's structurally-forced ~100% -- consistent with genuinely random addressing rather than a mapping artifact
